evidence.quote: apparet Fuldensem et Gothanum si non ex eodem archetypo descriptos eiusdem certe fuisse familiae
Tertiae denique familiae est tam, qui extat, codex Vaticanus 1860 (D) ... quam, qui ipse iam non superest ... quo usus est Paulus Diaconus
tertiae familiae archetypum propius ad A quam ad B accessisse consensus probat, qui est in corruptelis
codices C et A aperte ex archetypo communi iam erroneis lectionibus non adeo paucis inquinato descendunt, ut ex altero secunda familia et, ut mox videbimus, Paeanius pendent
quae lectiones in C eo inlatae sunt, quod codicum C archetypus correctus est ad exemplar quoddam secundae familiae
[Th. M.:] redire ea ad archetypa duo, ut ex altero pendeant tam Gothanus et Fuldensis (A) quam Paulini libri (C), ex altero tam Leidensis et Audomarensis (B) quam Paeanius

texts.notes: Three families A (GF), B (LO), C (D + Paulus' exemplar); A and C share an archetype against B+Paeanius. Droysen explains C's agreements with B by correction of C's archetype from a B-exemplar; Mommsen's bracketed note (Th. M.) rejects that contamination but keeps the same two-archetype division. F is lost (known via Sylburg); P and Paean. are indirect, so analysis witnesses of branch 2 are only L and O.

evidence.quote: Historiae Romanae codicum ... duo sunt genera, quae potissimum hiatu libri XV inter se distinguuntur
Codices Bambergensis et Vaticanus quamvis non ex eodem archetypo descripti tamen in omnibus gravioribus et hiatibus et erroribus consentiunt, ut eorum consensus pro uno codice haberi possit
[Berolinensis] errores librariorum, qui codices H et V exaraverunt, ... plerumque evitavit, in gravioribus omnibus ab eorum parte stat
Laurentiani et Vaticani communem originem et hiatus communes et errores iidem, praeterea interpolationes nonnullae demonstrant
[Monacensis] ut eius archetypus prioris familiae fuisse videatur sed suppletus et passim correctus ad codicem aliquem generis secundi

texts.notes: Two genera: hiantes (H V, + B) vs integri (N Z). M is placed by the editor in the first family but corrected from the second (contaminated across the top) and used only for books XI-XVI, as is B. Mommsen's bracketed footnote (p. XXXII n. 14) suggests the second genus may owe the book XV passage to Landolfus, i.e. it questions which family is interpolated but not the division. Books I-X are printed on pages facing Eutropius, so text_lines interleave with Eutropius and Paeanius.
